source.section: Schedule M line 47 Senior Citizen Deduction columns (a)-(d) (PDF p.6; instructions PDF p.29; example PDF p.30; PDF p.23 'Taxpayers over age 65 or disabled'; Tax Division page: 'You receive the higher of the $8,000 modification or the sum of various itemized decreasing modifications'); Schedule M line 32 Military Retirement Modification (PDF p.5; instructions PDF p.28; PDF p.22 'Certain State and Federal Retirement Systems'); Schedule M line 34 Social Security Benefits, 100% at or under the AGI limit and 65% above it for 2025 (PDF p.5; instructions PDF p.28; PDF p.17; Tax Division Social Security Modification page); IT-140 lines 1-8 (PDF p.3; instructions PDF p.26: exemptions 2,000 each, line 7 floored at zero); Rate Schedules I and II (PDF p.37); Tax Table (PDF p.38 on)

worked: Single, age 67, military retirement 3,000 and taxable Social Security together under 8,000: line 47 tops them up to 8,000. Projection: military 3,000 in full plus the larger of Social Security and (8,000 - 3,000). filer born 1958-04-04, age 67 at December 31, 2025. Federal taxable Social Security (IRS worksheet, given): other income 28,000.00 + half of benefits 2,000.00 = provisional income 30,000.00; 50% x (30,000.00 - 25,000.00) = 2,500.00, limited to half the benefits 2,000.00: 2,000.00. Federal AGI (given) = private pension 25,000.00 + military retirement 3,000.00 + taxable Social Security 2,000.00 = 30,000.00. Federal taxable income (given, not tested) = 30,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 aged 65 or older = 12,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). IT-140 line 1 federal AGI 30,000.00. Schedule M additions lines 51-58 none; IT-140 line 2 0.00. Schedule M Column A: line 32 military retirement 3,000.00 (in full, no cap); line 34(a) total benefits 4,000.00, (b) exempt for federal 2,000.00, (c) taxable 2,000.00; federal AGI 30,000.00 does not exceed 50,000.00, so line 34 = 2,000.00 (100%); line 47 (age 67): column (c) income not on lines 35-46 = 30,000.00, limited to 8,000.00: 8,000.00; column (d) lines 29-34 = 5,000.00; line 47 = 8,000.00 - 5,000.00 = 3,000.00; line 49 = 8,000.00. Line 50 total subtractions = 8,000.00. Projection (per person): The filer: Social Security subtraction 2,000.00; age 65 deduction = lesser of (8,000.00 - military retirement 3,000.00) and own income 30,000.00 = 5,000.00; best_of_group wv_line_47 keeps the larger, 5,000.00 (wv_senior_citizen_deduction). Projection subtractions total 8,000.00, the same as line 50. IT-140 line 3 subtractions 8,000.00; line 4 West Virginia AGI = 30,000.00 + 0.00 - 8,000.00 = 22,000.00. Line 5 Low-Income Earned Income Exclusion: federal AGI over 10,000, none. Line 6 exemptions 1 x 2,000.00 = 2,000.00. Line 7 taxable income = 22,000.00 - 2,000.00 = 20,000.00. Line 8 tax by Rate Schedule I (PDF p.37) bands: 2.22% x 10,000.00 = 222 + 2.96% x 10,000.00 = 296; total 518 = 518.00. The Tax Table row 20,000 to under 20,100 (PDF p.38 on) gives 519; expected keeps the schedule formula on the exact income. No Family Tax Credit (Modified Federal AGI above the table limits); credits 0.00; state income tax 518.00.
accepted_approximations: Tax below 100,000 of taxable income is figured on the exact income, where the booklet uses a Tax Table row's midpoint rounded to the whole dollar. Other tax is also rounded to the whole dollar in the booklet.
